items_missed: Called the customer by the wrong name on the third line of the call — 'Hello, Jeff. Good morning' — after Dev had just introduced himself

Agenda statement had no timeframe and no roadmap through pricing — 'I just need to gather details for this move in order for me to give you an on point estimate' covers the details half only, with no '10 to 15 minutes' and no walk-through-pricing promise
Never confirmed the origin address or either zip code out loud
Never asked what floor the origin apartment is on or whether there is elevator access there (unit 421 implies a 4th floor and he never checked)
Never asked about special considerations — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns — on a move between two apartment complexes
Never asked about parking, loading zones, dock access, or COI requirements at either complex
Never asked the moving-stressor question; 'any question or clarification regarding the moving process in general?' is not the same thing
No 'pricing is super simple' opener
No Worries Damage Coverage never explained — 'insurances' was named only as a competitor hidden fee, never as our $2,000 per-move coverage
Meet Your Mover never mentioned
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — notable on a customer who cared specifically about arrival window and traffic
Never explained that the clock starts on-site when the contract opens
Never explained 15-minute prorated increments after the 2.5-hour minimum — the single most relevant policy detail for a customer with a hard $500 ceiling
Never stated the 2.5-hour minimum proactively; the customer raised it first

NEVER DELIVERED THE ESTIMATE — said 'Before I go over pricing structure and estimate, do you have any question' and then, after the customer's traffic question, booked the job without ever returning to it
Never stated how many movers or trucks would be on the job
Never gave a typical time range for a one-bedroom apartment move
Never explained walk distance as a time variable at either building
Never explained bed-frame disassembly/reassembly as a time factor (only that there is no fee for it)

Entire Save Your Ass section absent — no 'prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill', no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, on a customer who volunteered 'I'm really honestly trying to budget $500, that's how much I have'
No bolded key-details list or 'reply with any corrections' framing for the confirmation email — only 'everything will be on the email'
Never gave business hours or a direct way to reach us beyond 'give us a callback'
No Ecobox referral despite the customer self-packing 7–8 boxes
No 60¢/lb baseline insurance explanation
top_strength: The no-hidden-fees rebuttal was the best piece of selling in either call this run. Facing a live competitor quote of $199 against our $204, Arden did not discount — he reframed: 'double-check if they have any hidden fees... their hourly rate might sound cheaper, however they're gonna surprise you with disassembling fees, staircase fees, transportation fees, gas fees, insurances and taxes. For us it's a flat $204, no extra charges, whatever time is accumulated, that's only what you pay for.' He also front-loaded no-deposit and free-rescheduling before the customer ever had to ask, hunted a Sunday promo rate to try to close the $5 gap, and explained packing pricing with a concrete, believable example (kitchen at roughly an hour and a half plus about $80 in supplies, charged at the same hourly rate). Inventory work was careful too — he circled back and re-confirmed the full item list, caught the missing desk, and screened for safes, pianos, and gym equipment.
coaching_note: Arden, you out-sold a cheaper competitor and closed the booking in ten minutes, and then you left the most important thing on the table: you never actually gave the estimate. Your exact words were 'I think I'm all good with my estimate sir. Before I go over pricing structure and estimate, do you have any question' — the customer asked about traffic, you scheduled the window, and the estimate never happened. Dev is on the books believing his move fits inside $500 with no idea how many movers are coming, how long we think it will take, or that time bills in 15-minute increments past the 2.5-hour minimum. It should have sounded like: 'For a one-bedroom with a couch, bed, TV stand, desk and about eight boxes, we'd send two movers and one truck, and I'd estimate three to three and a half hours door to door — the clock starts on-site when we open the contract, there's a two-and-a-half-hour minimum, and after that we bill in 15-minute increments, so at $204 you're looking at roughly $610 to $715. Does that make sense?' Second priority: the Save Your Ass speech was the answer to his budget problem and you skipped it entirely. When a customer tells you $500 is all he has, that is your cue — 'Here's how you control the bill: get everything into boxes and out of drawers before we arrive, pull the photos off the walls, consolidate the small stuff into one room, and take a carload over yourself. Every trip you make is time we don't bill.' LIVE BUSINESS RISK, and this is the part I want reviewed: instead of the prep speech you coached him to cut the crew off mid-job — 'if you think two and a half hour, you're good with two and a half hour and they're not yet done... you can just tell them, okay I only need two and a half hour for this, I'm gonna move the rest so they can prioritize just the big stuff.' That is telling a customer to accept an incomplete move to protect a budget, and it is a service-failure and review risk on a job we already booked. Second risk: you listed 'insurances' as a competitor hidden fee and told him it is 'already included or inclusive in the hourly rate' without ever explaining No Worries is capped at $2,000 per move over a 60¢/lb baseline — he may now believe his belongings are fully covered without limit. Third, smaller: he said he may call back to switch to Thursday, so confirm the rate holds on the new day. And check the recording on the open — the transcript has you greeting him as 'Jeff' right after he gave you his name.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and consultative with genuine acknowledgment of pushback ('Of course, I understand sir') and a customer who stayed comfortable and said 'that's perfect', held back from a 5 by scripted-sounding stretches, heavy filler, and the wrong-name misfire at the open.
